discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 211023
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
623 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dense fog is expected this morning, particularly along and
  east of Interstate 69. More patchy fog is possible tonight 
  with the greatest chances across northeast Indiana and 
  northwest Ohio. Some locally dense fog is possible again early
  Thursday morning.

- Dry weather will continue through the weekend with
  temperatures slightly above normal. Temperatures are expected
  to cool to slightly below normal by next Tuesday and
  Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 320 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

Satellite imagery early this morning depicts an expansive area of 
stratus/fog across northwest Ohio, with widespread dense fog 
developing across south central Lower Michigan and northwest Ohio. 
Weak easterly flow associated with eastern portions of low level 
anticyclone will support westward migration of this stratus/fog into 
far northeast Indiana over the next several hours. A Dense Fog 
Advisory has issued earlier this morning for Hillsdale Co MI and all 
of NW Ohio counties, and based on current trends, a westward 
expansion will likely be required. With expansive low level 
anticyclone in place and very weak low level flow, diurnal 
mixing will likely be slow to erode stratus/fog, with areas of 
fog persisting through the 14 to 15Z timeframe.

Otherwise for today will be monitoring the progress of a progressive 
mid/upper level short wave trough across the Upper Midwest this
morning as it reaches the western Great Lakes region. A narrow 
axis of mid level moisture/patchy mid level clouds will likely 
remain north of the local area while another area of mid clouds 
associated with mid level short wave progressing through mean 
upper ridging will largely remain displaced to the west from the
Central Plains to the Mid MS Valley. A persistence forecast 
largely utilized for high temperature forecast today as little 
thermal advections have been noted over past 24 hours with 
similar poor mixing profiles today and similar good amounts of
insolation.

Passage of the Great Lakes short wave this evening will allow for 
reinforcement and southwestward shift to low level anticyclone 
across the region. This should yield a weak northeasterly low level 
flow profile for tonight which once again raises the question of 
some enhancement to fog development downwind of eastern Great Lakes. 
Given northeast trajectories, greatest confidence in fog development 
tonight is far NE IN/NW OH mainly along and south of US Route 24, 
but some patchy fog will be possible once again for many areas east 
of I-69. THe fog may become locally dense once again early Thursday 
morning.

A stable wave pattern will maintain through the first part of the 
weekend with an eventual shift of longwave upper ridge axis 
east of the local area by 2nd half of the weekend. This should 
allow for Sunday to realize the warmest temperatures of the 
period in the low to mid 70s. Longwave predictability begins to 
break down early next week with large discrepancies in how 
phasing is depicted with western CONUS closed upper height 
perturbations among various deterministic/ensemble guidance. 
Some indications that stronger frontal forcing will develop 
northwest of the local area late weekend/early next week as 
southwest CONUS upper wave pushes east and dampens, but given 
uncertainty in progression and depth of this wave as it reaches 
central CONUS argues for maintenance of mainly dry forecast at 
this time with expectation that frontal forcing will wane
through time. Blended guidance idea of trend back to cooler 
conditions early to mid next week still appears reasonable.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 620 AM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

The combination of satellite/sfc obs/web cams across northeast
Indiana indicate a westward drifting area of dense fog across
northeast Indiana. Cigs of 200 feet or less and vsbys down to
1/4SM have approached the KFWA vicinity as of 10Z, and expecting
these conditions to hold through 14Z before improving. IFR/vsbys
will likely hold through mid morning before improvement back to
VFR conditions due to poor mixing in this synoptic setup. At
KSBN, fog is expected to be more patchy in nature, but cannot
rule out a period of brief IFR vsbys in fog early this morning. 
An upper level short wave trough will track across the Great 
Lakes region today allowing for a reinforcement and southwest 
expansion of a low level anticyclone across the Mid MS River 
Valley. This will keep a weak gradient in place through this 
forecast valid period. With weak low level northeasterlies given
the re-orientation of the anticyclone today, flow trajectories 
will be supportive of some more stratus and fog developing 
across eastern Great Lakes tonight and building west again. Best
chances of more widespread coverage may be just south of KFWA 
however.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

     017-018-026-027-034.

     004-005-015-016-024-025.
MI...Dense Fog Advisory until 10 AM EDT this morning for MIZ079>081.
MARINE...None.

&&

spc.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of producing large hail, a few tornadoes, and damaging winds are expected today and tonight across parts of Arizona and vicinity. Isolated severe gusts and perhaps a tornado may also occur along the central/southern California Coast.
spc.text:
SPC AC 211230

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0730 AM CDT Wed Oct 21 2026

   Valid 211300Z - 221200Z

   ...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   ARIZONA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms capable of producing large hail, a few
   tornadoes, and damaging winds are expected today and tonight across
   parts of Arizona and vicinity. Isolated severe gusts and perhaps a
   tornado may also occur along the central/southern California Coast.

   ...Southwest...
   Ongoing thunderstorms across central/northern AZ early this morning
   are being aided by large-scale ascent associated with a strong
   southwesterly mid/upper-level jet. This activity should continue to
   pose a threat for mainly isolated severe hail in the short term,
   with 40-50 kt of effective bulk shear aiding updraft organization
   and supercell potential in an otherwise weakly unstable environment
   (MUCAPE generally 500-1000 J/kg at the moment). Current expectations
   are for these thunderstorms to continue advancing northward into an
   even less unstable environment, but regenerative convection may
   persist for much of the morning as additional cells move over the
   Mogollon Rim.

   In the wake of this morning convection, an already unseasonably
   moist low-level airmass present across southern/central AZ is
   forecast to slowly spread northward across the lower CO River Valley
   and Mogollon Rim vicinity through the afternoon. Even with
   widespread cloudiness, filtered daytime heating will support gradual
   airmass destabilization and the development of up to 1000-1500 J/kg
   of MLCAPE across this region (locally stronger in central AZ), as
   convective inhibition becomes minimal by 18-20Z. Additional
   thunderstorms will likely develop across central/northern AZ in this
   time frame, as persistent forcing for ascent attendant to the
   mid/upper-level southwesterly jet remains over the Southwest.

   Strong deep-layer shear (40-55+ kt) will easily support supercells,
   with an associated threat for large hail. Greater instability is
   forecast with southward/westward extent in central AZ and southern
   NV, but lower thunderstorm coverage may exist in these areas. Still,
   a conditional risk for 2+ inch diameter hail remains apparent with
   splitting supercells given the rather favorable overlap of moderate
   instability and elongated/nearly straight hodographs at mid/upper
   levels. Occasional severe/damaging winds may also occur, but the
   tendency for convection to remain mostly discrete may limit
   clustering potential to some extent.

   The tornado threat with these supercells remains somewhat uncertain,
   as temperatures will remain fairly cool across northern AZ today.
   Even so, the risk for a few tornadoes may focus across parts of
   northwest/north-central AZ this afternoon and early evening, where
   greater low-level shear is forecast to reside amid generally
   east-southeasterly low-level winds. It should also be noted that
   multiple rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms appear likely
   today into tonight. Primary changes with this update were to extend
   the Slight Risk westward across northwest AZ/southeast NV/southwest
   UT mainly for large hail potential with supercells this
   afternoon/evening, and to expand the Marginal Risk in southern NV
   and western NM.

   ...Coastal Central/Southern California...
   A large, closed upper low over the eastern Pacific will approach the
   central CA Coast through the period, with a belt of strong southerly
   flow at mid levels expected to overspread coastal central/southern
   CA through the day. A low-topped line of convection may develop in
   response and impact this region during the afternoon/evening.
   Instability is forecast to remain minimal/shallow, and this activity
   may struggle to reach sufficient height for charge separation and
   lightning production. Still, given modestly enhanced flow and
   low-level shear, an isolated risk for severe gusts and perhaps a
   tornado may exist as this convection moves onshore.

   ..Gleason/Kerr.. 10/21/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1630Z

spc.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across the Southwest and Four Corners area on Thursday, with the greatest risk across parts of Arizona. All severe hazards will be possible.
spc.text:
SPC AC 210547

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1247 AM CDT Wed Oct 21 2026

   Valid 221200Z - 231200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PORTIONS OF
   CENTRAL ARIZONA INTO FAR WESTERN NEW MEXICO...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across the Southwest and
   Four Corners area on Thursday, with the greatest risk across parts
   of Arizona. All severe hazards will be possible.

   ...Synopsis...
   A broad longwave mid-level trough will traverse the western CONUS on
   Thursday, encouraging continued deep-layer ascent amid the northward
   advection of low-level moisture, promoting scattered to widespread
   thunderstorm development. At least isolated severe thunderstorms are
   possible spanning the Desert Southwest into the Great Basin given
   overlapping marginal buoyancy and widespread strong wind fields
   aloft. However, across portions of the Desert Southwest, an embedded
   mid-level impulse accompanied by a 500 mb speed max atop locally
   higher low-level moisture/instability may promote a more focused
   risk of severe thunderstorms.

   ...Desert Southwest into the Great Basin...
   Deep-layer ascent, combined with at least some degree of surface
   heating ahead of the broader upper trough, will support scattered
   thunderstorm development over the Great Basin during the afternoon.
   Largely unidirectional (southerly) tropospheric flow will yield
   highly elongated, straight hodographs and over 50 kts of effective
   bulk (speed) shear. Given 7 C/km mid-level lapse rates and around
   500 J/kg MLCAPE, transient supercells and small line segments will
   be the main storm modes, accompanied by an isolated severe gust/hail
   threat.

   Farther south into central AZ to far western NM, a 70+ kt 500 mb
   southwesterly speed max with 7+ C/km mid-level lapse rates will
   overspread southeasterly low-level flow and low to mid 60s F surface
   dewpoints. This ambient environment, as shown by forecast soundings,
   will yield modestly elongated hodographs, but with appreciable size
   and curvature at the low-levels. Given locally higher moisture, up
   to 1500 J/kg MLCAPE may be realized in tandem with 50+ kts of
   effective bulk shear and over 200 m2/s2 of effective SRH. While CAM
   guidance consensus depicts a complex storm mode and several
   potential cellular interactions, longer-lived, embedded supercell
   structures are possible. Should such storms develop, all severe
   hazards will be possible, including a couple of tornadoes.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/21/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.riskAtLaPorte: No thunderstorm or severe risk area
spc.summary: Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of central into southern New Mexico on Friday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 210723

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0223 AM CDT Wed Oct 21 2026

   Valid 231200Z - 241200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS PORTIONS OF
   CENTRAL INTO SOUTHERN NEW MEXICO...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of
   central into southern New Mexico on Friday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A broad longwave upper trough will impinge on the Rockies on Friday,
   supporting strong surface lee troughing along the High Plains.
   Continued northward advecting low-level moisture and deep-layer
   ascent accompanying the broad upper trough will support isolated to
   scattered thunderstorms all along the Rockies to the northern
   Plains. Across portions of the southern Rockies, locally richer
   moisture and associated instability, beneath stronger flow aloft,
   will support a risk for isolated severe thunderstorms.

   ...Portions of central into southern New Mexico...
   An embedded mid-level impulse and accompanying 50+ kt mid-level
   southwesterly speed max will graze the southern Rockies during by
   afternoon. By this time, surface heating of a low-level airmass
   comprising upper 50s F dewpoints and overspread by 7.5+ C/km
   mid-level lapse rates will yield over 1500 J/kg MLCAPE in spots.
   Scattered thunderstorms should initiate by afternoon, amid veering
   and strengthening flow with height. Forecast soundings show modest
   low-level hodograph curvature and up to 40 kts of effective bulk
   shear. This shear, along with the aforementioned buoyancy, should
   support a mix of multicells and supercells capable of producing
   isolated instances of severe hail and wind.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/21/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
